figures.caption: Same target and prespecified datasets. Crosses mark failed diagnostic gates; gate also checks rank-normalized R-hat. Minimum is across bulk/tail ESS of original hyperparameters and recovered functionals. ESS/second is omitted for resumed timings. These are development fits, not forecast accuracy results.

Dots are means of independent dataset losses; whiskers are +/-2 MCSE where at least two datasets contribute. Operational RMSE includes declared fallbacks. CRPS uses each method's qualified native distributions; marginal CRPS dots can involve different datasets. Use paired contrasts for direct comparisons.

Saved marginal interval coverage and proper interval scores averaged over eligible datasets, using a fixed model subset for legibility. Coverage is not simultaneous whole-field coverage, and small conditional populations do not establish calibration. The interval score jointly penalizes excessive width and missed observations.

Mean of saved dataset-level lead scores, without future-data assimilation. Bias is forecast mean minus observed response. Model subset is fixed for legibility; complete scores remain in the machine summaries. Exact operational/native dataset counts are in the preceding design and qualification table; native CRPS populations vary by model. No fit or forecast was recomputed.

Recorded costs averaged over the run's declared scenario/task mix; this is not machine-independent throughput. 0 jobs have incomplete compute accounting after infrastructure interruption; their recorded times are lower bounds. Failed scientific attempts remain in cost and operational populations. Process peak RSS is kept in raw receipts with its measurement scope.

Accuracy and recorded computational cost for the same declared jobs. Lower and left is preferable, but points have different qualification/fallback behavior; this plot is descriptive, not a Pareto-superiority test. Costs include tuning, final fitting, forecasting and saved-artifact serialization; lost work remains labeled incomplete.
